title: Black holes have a temperature, and small ones are hot
body: Hawking showed in 1974 that black holes radiate thermally, with temperature inversely proportional to mass. A stellar black hole sits far below the cosmic background and effectively never shrinks, but a hypothetical mountain-mass one would glow fiercely. The result fused gravity, quantum theory and thermodynamics in one formula, and its information paradox still organises research.
